cue_s02_c1_extracting_astrophysics_gravitationa 01 · INFERENCE Inference needs a likelihood Extracting astrophysics from gravitational waves means Bayesian inference over masses and spins — and that inference requires a noise likelihood.

cue_s02_c2_decades_field_assumed_noise_gaussian 02 · THE ASSUMPTION A convenient assumption For decades the field assumed detector noise is Gaussian and stationary, because it makes the likelihood tractable and cheap to evaluate.

cue_s02_c3_but_real_detectors_drift_over 03 · REALITY But real detectors are messy Sensitivity drifts over time, and data carry transient glitches and narrow, wandering spectral lines that violate the Gaussian model.

cue_s02_c4_these_handled_segment_segment_costly 04 · THE COST Costly fixes that can bias results With no generative model, artifacts are handled segment-by-segment with bespoke fixes. Famously, GW170817 landed right on a loud LIGO glitch.
